card.name: Words inside compound terms and dose phrases
card.fires_on: A word or piece in the middle of a compound phrase, where more of the phrase must follow. Examples are the unit after a number, a connector like plus or times, or an ordinal ending.

modes.label: Unit or schedule word
modes.description: A unit or frequency word inside a dose or regimen phrase, right after a number.
modes.example: Both the 1<< mg>>/mL and the 5 mg/mL formulations

modes.label: Connector in a pairing
modes.description: A linking word between two named items that are joined as one phrase.
modes.example: The WHI estrogen<< plus>> progestin substudy reported increased risks

modes.label: Ordinal or modifier in a hyphenated phrase
modes.description: A piece of a number or adjective that is followed by a hyphen and a noun.
modes.example: such late 18<<th>>-century writers as Phillis Wheatley.

card.plain: It fires partway through a compound phrase, such as a dose unit or a pairing, when the phrase is not yet finished.
